text:
alex: Heads-up 1: prototype for a "condensed replay" UI on rollouts page. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/efgh5678/condensed-replay (link) :mag:

maya: Nice. High-level goal? more vertical density or faster triage when debugging regressions?

alex: Both. Main idea: a narrow timeline bar with grouped micro-rollouts and an expandable inline replay that slides over the list rather than opening a full modal.

sam: Quick visual feedback: the grouped chevrons look cramped at small widths. Increase spacing and make hit targets >= 44px. Also add an explicit focus outline for keyboard users.

patrick: Accessibility: the chevron group should expose a button with aria-expanded toggling, and the replay slide should be announced. Example: `<div role="dialog" aria-modal="false" aria-label="Version replay">` and use `aria-live` for status updates.

maya: Microcopy proposal for the inline CTA: `View version replay 1 step through changes and traffic shifts.` Too long?

alex: Trim to `View version replay 1 step through changes.` Keep traffic details near the allocation controls.

patrick: On rollback defaults: ops asked for safer default. Recommend staged rollback 5% -> 25% over 15 minutes, with a clear tertiary action "Immediate 100%" that requires an extra confirmation.

sam: UX question: should the staged rollout be reversible mid-run? e.g., while a rollback canary is running let users abort to 100% or extend duration. I think yes, show inline controls next to active canary.

maya: For the allocation control, I'm thinking a compact segmented input with presets (1,5,10,25,100) and a tiny editable field for custom percent. Show an inline cost delta: `+~$0.03/min` or `latency +20ms`.

patrick: Keyboard interactions: presets focusable, arrow keys to cycle, Enter to select. For the editable percent, ensure `aria-valuenow` and `aria-valuetext` readout like `25 percent, est 2.1k req/min`.

sam: Implementation note: we can render the condensed timeline as an accessible SVG with grouped aria-labels like `3 events collapsed: 2 by jessica, 1 by ops` to help screen readers.

maya: Density rule: if > 15 events in 24h, collapse micro-rollouts (author same + <2% traffic) into a single group with a small badge `+N`. Expandable inline. Also provide a toggle `Always show micro-events` in user preferences.

alex: Nice. Also add a tiny legend: `Showing 12 events 2 collapsed` so users understand grouping.

patrick: A/B test copy idea: Variant A uses `Staged rollback (recommended)` as primary button, Variant B uses `Rollback (staged)` and shows a recommended badge. Track clicks, aborts, and re-rollbacks.

sam: Keyboard shortcut suggestion: `[` then `r` to open replay when focused on a rollout entry. Need to audit conflicts.

maya: One more: when replaying diffs, include a small timestamp scrubber and a `jump to snapshot` control. If backend stores diffs only, we should provide guard rails in UI when reconstruction takes longer. Show a spinner with `Reconstructing state...` message.

alex: Backend will expose `replay_index` endpoint; frontend can request nearest snapshot + diffs for playback. If long running, show retry/abort options.

patrick: Accessibility test plan bullets: 1) Tab-only traversal covers group expand/collapse, open replay, step frames, and close dialog. 2) NVDA/VoiceOver reads group summary and replay announcements. 3) High-contrast theme passes 4.5:1 for labels and status chips.

maya: Action items: @maya update Figma with larger hit targets, segmented presets, and the condensed group state (due EOD). @sam spike an SVG prototype + keyboard handlers (branch next week). @patrick formalize the ARIA attributes and acceptance test steps. @alex coordinate backend API for snapshots.

aria-bot: Reminder: Design critique scheduled Thu 10am. Add the ARIA checklist to the PR template.

maya: Will do, pinging when updated :thumbsup:

sam: I'll post a demo link once the branch is up.

alex: Thanks everyone. Compact but discoverable is the goal 1 appreciate the a11y focus. :rocket:
